nodes.name: CP Acid Pretreatment
nodes.procedure: CP was soaked in a mixed solution of concentrated hydrochloric acid and concentrated nitric acid with a volume ratio of 3:1 for 24 h as pretreatment. The acid-treated CP was then washed several times and dried.

nodes.name: Ga Electroplating
nodes.procedure: NaOH solution (0.5 M) and 1 mL liquid Ga were poured into a beaker. The wire connected to the positive pole of the direct power supply was immersed in liquid Ga, while the CP, serving as the negative electrode, was immersed into the solution. The voltage was set to 8 V and electroplating was carried out for 10 s. The CPs were washed with ethanol and dried.

unit_operations.name: Electroplating
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: The voltage of the direct current power supply was initially set to 8 V. Electroplating was then carried out for 10 s.

nodes.name: Nitrate Adsorption
nodes.procedure: CP/Ga was immersed in a mixed-metal nitrate ethanol solution (Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Zn) with a total concentration of 1 M for 5 s and dried.

nodes.name: Thermal Treatment to Core-Shell HEO
nodes.procedure: The metal salt-attached CP/Ga samples were heated in a tube furnace in a 97% N2 and 3% O2 atmosphere. The temperature was raised to 650 °C within 30 min and maintained for 2 h. It was then cooled down to room temperature within 30 min.

nodes.name: Synthesis of CP/HEO Control
nodes.procedure: The acid-treated CP was immersed in the mixed metal-nitrate solution for 5 s and dried. Finally, the CP was heated in a tube furnace with the same sintering parameters (650 °C for 2 h).
nodes.source_text: The acid-treated CP was then immersed in the mixed solution for 5 s and dried. Finally, the CP was heated in a tube furnace using the same heating process as preparing CP/Ga2O3 to obtain CP/HEO.

nodes.name: Synthesis of CP/Ga2O3 Control
nodes.procedure: CP/Ga was heated in a tube furnace in a 97% N2 and 3% O2 atmosphere. The temperature was raised to 650 °C within 30 min and maintained for 2 h.
nodes.source_text: CP/Ga2O3 was prepared by heating CP/Ga in a tube furnace in a 97% N2 and 3% O2 atmosphere. The temperature was raised to 650 °C within 30 min and maintained for 2 h.

nodes.name: Preparation of Mixed Nitrate Solution
nodes.procedure: A mixed solution of manganese nitrate, iron nitrate, cobalt nitrate, nickel nitrate, and zinc nitrate in ethanol was prepared, with a total concentration of 1 M.
nodes.source_text: A mixed solution of manganese nitrate, iron nitrate, cobalt nitrate, nickel nitrate, and zinc nitrate in ethanol was prepared, with a total concentration of 1 M.

nodes.name: Synthesis on Alternative Substrates
nodes.procedure: Powders of TiO2, Al2O3, and CuO were dispersed in ethanol by ultrasonication, and suspensions of the three were dropped on CP and dried. Then, the mixed-metal salt solutions were dropped onto the CP. After drying, the CPs were heated at 650 °C for 2 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms the cubic spinel structure of the HEO shell and monoclinic Ga2O3. A shift of 0.7° to the left in the spinel HEO peak at 62.5° indicates tensile strain, and Rietveld refinement shows a lattice expansion of 0.124 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the peak of CP/Ga2O3@HEO at 62.5 ... shifts to the left by 0.7° ... tensile strain effect exerted by the Ga2O3 substrate on the HEO shell, causing an increase in its crystal plane spacing

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms the chemical states of Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, and Zn (e.g., NiFe2O4, Co3O4) and shows that the surface valence states are identical for HEO grown on Ga2O3 versus HEO grown on carbon paper, indicating no ligand effect changes to the surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The surface chemical states of each element in the HEO film formed on Ga2O3 and those in the HEO formed on CP are the same, without obvious peak shift, which proves that different substrates do not affect the surface valence states of HEO.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance (Cdl) was used to calculate the Electrochemical Active Surface Area (ECSA), yielding 1070.50 cm2 for the Ga2O3-supported catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cdl values of CP/Ga2O3@HEO ... are 42.82 ... ECSA values of the three are calculated to be 1070.50

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy shows that CP/Ga2O3@HEO has a low charge-transfer resistance (Rct) of approximately 0.55 Ohm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ohmic Rct values of CP/Ga2O3@HEO is fitted to be 0.55 ± 0.07 Ω.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS analysis of the electrolyte after OER stability testing shows low concentrations of leached Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, and Zn (0.10–0.13 mg/L).
nodes.evidence_snippet: leaching of elements in the electrolyte was studied by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS), where the concentrations of Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Zn were 0.12, 0.13, 0.10, 0.11, 0.10 mg/L.

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ Raman shows redshifts in characteristic bands with increasing temperature, attributed to tight bonding and tensile strain exerted by the Ga2O3 substrate on the HEO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: noticeable redshifts in the Raman characteristic bands of HEO were observed ... tensile strain effect is exerted by Ga2O3 on HEO

nodes.characterization_summary: Thermogravimetry (TG) was used to experimentally measure and compare the binding interactions (work of separation) between HEO and Ga2O3 versus HEO and carbon paper.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The work of separation between Ga2O3 and HEO, as well as that between CP and HEO, was also experimentally measured using TG... (Supplementary Fig. 24).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping and line scans confirm a core-shell structure with Ga in the core and a uniform distribution of Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, and Zn in the shell, with shell thicknesses ranging from a few to several tens of nanometers.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The linear scanning profile exhibits a core-shell structure, where the main metallic element inside the sphere is Ga, and the metallic elements in the outer shell of the sphere are Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, and Zn ... thicknesses of the shells range from a few nanometers to several tens of nanometers.
